newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Sydney Olympics boss Hemmerling resign.
newsitem.headline: Sydney Olympics boss Hemmerling resign.

text.p: Sydney's 2000 Olympics organising committee lost its third senior figure in a year on Wednesday with the resignation of chief executive Mal Hemmerling.

Hemmerling, who held the post since August 1995, had resigned "to pursue other career interests", the office of the New South Wales state government's Olympics Minister Michael Knight said in a statement.
The Sydney Organising Committe for the Olympic Games (SOCOG) has been plagued by the loss of senior personnel during the past two years.
Businessman John Iliffe resigned as SOCOG president in September, his predecessor Gary Pemberton stepped down last March, and a string of executives has also left.
The 15-member SOCOG board will meet on Friday morning to appoint a replacement for Hemmerling, who previously ran the Australian Formula One Grand Prix in Adelaide for 10 years.
Local media reported former top Federal government bureacrat Sandy Hollway, appointed last December as one of two effective deputies to Hemmerling, was likely to win the position.
Earlier on Wednesday, Australian Olympic Committee (AOC) president John Coates said he would step down as chairman of troubled casino operator Reef Casino Trust.
Coates has been criticised for investing a large part of the AOC's funds in the Cairns, Queensland, casino, which has consistently failed to match its own profit and revenue forecasts.
The AOC faces a big loss on its A$7 million (US$5.5 million) investment, with casino trust units plunging in value from about A$1.40 when it listed in late 1995 to 16.5 cents on Wednesday.
